{{Short description|Mathematical algorithm}}
'''Wichmann–Hill''' is a [[pseudorandom number generator]] proposed in 1982 by [[Brian Wichmann]] and David Hill.<ref>{{Cite journal
 |title=Algorithm AS 183: An Efficient and Portable Pseudo-Random Number Generator
 |last1=Wichmann |first1=Brian A.  |last2=Hill |first2=I. David
 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series C (Applied Statistics)
 |volume=31 |issue=2 |year=1982 |pages=188–190
 |doi=10.2307/2347988  
|jstor=2347988 }}</ref> It consists of three [[linear congruential generator]]s with different [[Prime number|prime]] moduli, each of which is used to produce a [[uniform distribution (continuous)|uniformly distributed]] number between 0 and 1. These are summed, modulo 1, to produce the result.<ref>{{Cite journal
 |title=Remark AS R58: A Remark on Algorithm AS 183. An Efficient and Portable Pseudo-Random Number Generator
 |last1=McLeod |first1=A. Ian
 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series C (Applied Statistics)
 |volume=34 |issue=2 |year=1985 |pages=198–200
 |doi=10.2307/2347378
 |jstor=2347378 |quote=Wichmann and Hill (1982) claim that their generator RANDOM will produce uniform pseudorandom numbers which are strictly greater than zero and less than one.  However, depending on the precision of the machine, some zero values may be produced due to rounding error.
}}  The problem occurs with [[single-precision floating point]] when [[rounding]] to zero.</ref>

Summing three generators produces a pseudorandom sequence with cycle exceeding {{val|6.95|e=12}}.<ref>{{Cite journal
 |title=Correction: Algorithm AS 183: An Efficient and Portable Pseudo-Random Number Generator
 |last1=Wichmann |first1=Brian  |last2=Hill |first2=David
 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series C (Applied Statistics)
 |volume=33 |issue=1 |year=1984 |page=123
 |doi=10.2307/2347676 
|jstor=2347676 }}</ref>  Specifically, the moduli are 30269, 30307 and 30323, producing periods of 30268, 30306 and 30322.  The overall period is the [[least common multiple]] of these: 30268×30306×30322/4 = {{val|6953607871644}}.  This has been confirmed by a [[brute-force search]].<ref>{{cite web
 |last1=Rikitake |first1=Kenji
 |title=AS183 PRNG algorithm internal state calculator in C
 |website=[[GitHub]]
 |date=16 March 2017
 |url=https://github.com/jj1bdx/as183-c
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal
 |title=Remark ASR 61: A Remark on Algorithm AS 183. An Efficient and Portable Pseudo-Random Number Generator
 |last1=Zeisel |first1=H.
 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series C (Applied Statistics)
 |volume=35 |issue=1 |year=1986 |page=98
 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-9876.1986.tb01945.x |jstor=2347876 |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/2347876
 |quote=Wichmann and Hill (1982) suggested a pseudo-random generator based on summation of pseudo-random numbers based on summation of pseudo-random numbers generated by multiplicative congruential methods.  This, however, is not more than an efficient method to implement a multiplicative congruential generator with a cycle length much greater than the maximal integer.  Using the [[Chinese Remainder Theorem]] (see e.g. [[The Art of Computer Programming|Knuth, 1981]]) you can prove that you will obtain the same results using only one multiplicative congruential generator {{math|1=''X''<sub>''n''+1</sub> = ''α''⋅''X<sub>n</sub>'' modulo ''m''}} with {{math|1=''α'' = 1655&thinsp;54252&thinsp;64690}}, {{math|1=''m'' = 2781&thinsp;71856&thinsp;04309}}.  The original version, however, is still necessary to make a generator with such lengthy constants work on ordinary computer arithmetic.
|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Implementation ==
The following [[pseudocode]] is for implementation on machines capable of integer arithmetic up to {{val|fmt=commas|5212632}}:

 [r, s1, s2, s3] = '''function'''(''s1'', ''s2'', ''s3'') '''is'''
     ''// s1, s2, s3 should be random from 1 to 30,000. Use clock if available.''
     ''s1'' := mod(171 × ''s1'', 30269)
     ''s2'' := mod(172 × ''s2'', 30307)
     ''s3'' := mod(170 × ''s3'', 30323)
 
     ''r'' := mod(''s1''/30269.0 + ''s2''/30307.0 + ''s3''/30323.0, 1)

For machines limited to 16-bit signed integers, the following equivalent code only uses numbers up to {{val|fmt=commas|30323}}:

 [r, s1, s2, s3] = '''function'''(''s1'', ''s2'', ''s3'') '''is'''
     ''// s1, s2, s3 should be random from 1 to 30,000. Use clock if available.''
     ''s1'' := 171 × mod(''s1'', 177) − 2 × floor(''s1'' / 177)
     ''s2'' := 172 × mod(''s2'', 176) − 35 × floor(''s2'' / 176)
     ''s3'' := 170 × mod(''s3'', 178) − 63 × floor(''s3'' / 178)
 
     ''r'' := mod(s1/30269 + s2/30307 + s3/30323, 1)

The seed values <code>s1</code>, <code>s2</code> and <code>s3</code> must be initialized to non-zero values.
